ground_truth.text: Parameterising the URL scheme in the release workflow's api() helper dropped curl's --tlsv1.2 floor (only --proto "$proto" remains), so the request carrying the release token no longer enforces a minimum TLS version.

The install script, the 65 spec and the timing harness say the REQ_RELEASE_BASE and REQ_CURL_PROTO overrides are test-only and never set by any shipped YAML, but the timing harness sets both, and over a LAN http server URL the instance-wide read token crosses that hop in clear. The statements about who may set them are false.

findings.text: Sensitive information exposure: when the runner's `github.server_url` is `http://`, `release.yml`'s `api()` now sends the token used to create/upload releases unencrypted over the LAN (the previous code forced `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2`). The PR documents this as an accepted LAN trade-off, and the https path also loses the explicit `--tlsv1.2` floor. Confirm the token's scope is minimal and the LAN hop is trusted, or keep the token-bearing path on HTTPS only.
findings.title: security concern

findings.text: The new explanatory comment quotes the literal host `https://<private-host>`, but `tests/release_workflow.rs` adds `forbid(RELEASE, &text, "<private-host>", ...)`. If `forbid` is a plain substring check over the file text (as the surrounding `require`/`forbid` helpers suggest), the test will match this comment and `the_release_builds_with_the_script_that_proves_the_binary` fails, blocking CI. Reference "the public tailnet name" without the literal host, or have `forbid` skip comment lines. Uncertain: the helper implementation is not in the diff; if it strips comments this is only a documentation inconsistency.
findings.title: Test/comment conflict

findings.text: Switching the fixed `=https` proto to a `$proto` variable also dropped the explicit `--tlsv1.2` floor. On the https branch this weakens the transport the `Authorization` token rides on (curl will now accept whatever TLS its build permits, e.g. 1.0/1.1), and it diverges from `examples/install-req.sh`, which keeps `--tlsv1.2` alongside the variable `--proto`. `--tlsv1.2` is a no-op for an `http://` URL, so it can stay unconditional.
findings.title: security

findings.text:
The new test in `tests/release_workflow.rs` asserts that the release workflow text does not contain
`<private-host>`, but this added comment embeds that literal host name, so the `forbid` check will fail.
Reword the comment so it explains the same fact without spelling out the public host.
findings.title: Remove forbidden host literal from comment
findings.code:
# The URL THIS RUNNER reaches Forgejo at (its own server URL: the one checkout uses), not the
# public tailnet name: the runner is a LAN container with no tailnet DNS, so
# https://<private-host> does not resolve there (first dispatch: "Could not resolve host").

findings.text: Two problems with the new timing pins. (a) The needle is the whole shell expression verbatim, so a behaviour-preserving rewrite (building the base in a variable first, or using `${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}` as release.yml does) turns the test red even though the override is still correct — it pins formatting, not the rule. (b) Nothing pins `REQ_CURL_PROTO`: deleting the entire `case $GITHUB_SERVER_URL` block keeps this test green, yet the prebuilt timing would then fall back to the script's `=https` default and fail at dispatch on an `http://` runner. Mutation-check the http branch by pinning that `REQ_CURL_PROTO` is set from the server URL (e.g. require the `=http` branch or the variable derivation), rather than pinning the exact base literal.
findings.title: test

findings.text:
Replacing the hard-coded `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2` with a scheme-derived `--proto "$proto"` also drops the
`--tlsv1.2` minimum, so an https server may be negotiated down to an older TLS version on token-bearing
requests. Keep `--tlsv1.2` (it is ignored for plain-http transfers) so the TLS floor is preserved when https is used.
findings.title: Preserve TLS 1.2 minimum floor
